Independent code review (8-angle finder pass, medium effort) surfaced 9 candidates, 8 verified real (1 REFUTED — a claimed duplicate of lib/action-link-style.ts's primaryActionLinkStyle, which turned out technically unable to support the :disabled/:focus-visible states real <button> elements need). Most severe: buttons re-enabled via the component's finally block immediately after firing router.refresh() (which returns void and isn't awaited), letting a rushed or double-clicking user fire a since-invalid transition before the refresh had actually landed — fixed by having the component own a local status state, updated in the same batched render as clearing pending, so the rendered button set is never stale relative to whether it's enabled. Also fixed: an unguarded ALLOWED_TRANSITIONS[status] lookup that could throw on an out-of-union status (now falls back to no actions); a silent network-failure catch with no logging (now logs via console.error, closing the same blind-spot class the Project Switcher review already fixed once); a self-contradicting doc comment in page.tsx; a stale claim in dashboard-web-project-detail.md (addended, not rewritten, preserving that document's own historical accuracy); a duplicated .error CSS class (extracted into a new shared error-message.module.css both project-form.module.css and project-status-actions.module.css now compose from); and a duplicated ProjectStatus type alias (now imports the existing ProjectStatusFilter from lib/projects.ts). gates.notes: Cross-domain session-exchange fix for Google SSO login (branch fix-cross-domain-session-exchange, PR #35). Fixes a real production bug: dashboard-api's Google OIDC callback set its session cookie and redirected straight to WEB_APP_ORIGIN's root, but that cookie is host-only to dashboard-api's own *.vercel.app domain (no Domain attribute, no shared parent domain with dashboard-web's separate project) — it was never actually sent on the browser's subsequent navigation to dashboard-web, so every login silently looped back to /auth/sign-in. Not a SameSite bug — SameSite=None is already correct for the cross-site requests this app makes to dashboard-api; the broken case is the browser's own top-level navigation away from it. Fixed with a session-exchange mechanism: a short-lived (60s), single-use, opaque exchange code (migration 00046, session_exchange_codes) redeemed server-to-server against a new POST /auth/exchange endpoint, minting dashboard-web its own independent first-party session (not a relay of the original raw token). Independent code review (high effort, 8-angle finder pass) surfaced 11 candidates, 10 CONFIRMED — most severe: splitting one login into two independent sessions meant 'Sign out' only ever revoked the rarely-used dashboard-api-side session, never the dashboard-web-side one getServerSession() actually authenticates every page against; fixed with a new DELETE /auth/session route in dashboard-web forwarding the whole Cookie header to dashboard-api's /auth/logout with an explicit Origin header. 9 of 10 CONFIRMED findings fixed and re-validated (also: an unguarded exchange-code issue() call that could leak a raw 500 with a session cookie already staged; the active session being stamped with the exchange call's own ipHash/userAgent instead of the real browser's; a missing auth_events record for the session actually in use; an unguarded response.json(); a cookie-name drift risk between the two apps; a hardcoded secure:true with no local-dev override; a duplicated redirect-to-error literal; an extra DB round-trip in redeem()). The 10th (POST /auth/exchange has no OriginCheckGuard/shared secret beyond the code's own entropy/single-use/60s TTL) was left as accepted, tracked debt, flagged explicitly for the second-role reviewer. Security review (run separately, against the fixed branch) found 0 findings above threshold — one candidate (best-effort logout not checking response.ok before clearing the local cookie) was identified and adversarially verified, rejected at 2/10 confidence. gates.notes: /auth/exchange error-masking fix (branch fix-auth-exchange-error-masking, PR #36). Diagnosing a 2026-08-19 sign-in incident (a login racing migration 00046, producing a Postgres 42P01 undefined_table error) surfaced that every failure path in the session-exchange flow -- both GoogleAuthController#callback's sessionExchange.issue() catch block (dashboard-api) and dashboard-web's /auth/exchange route's redirectToAuthError() helper -- redirected to /auth/error?reason=expired regardless of the real failure class, masking a genuine backend error as a routine expired-code case. Fixed by splitting the taxonomy into reason=expired (genuinely expired/invalid: missing OIDC transaction cookie, missing exchange-code param, backend 400) and a new reason=error (everything else). Diagnostics-only -- no change to session cookies, SameSite, OriginCheckGuard, or actual success/failure outcomes, only which message is shown and what gets logged. gates.notes: AuthErrorReason shared-type fix (branch fix-auth-error-reason-shared-type, PR #37). Closes one of PR #36's own 5 accepted-debt findings: the /auth/error reason taxonomy (expired/access_denied/error) was declared independently in dashboard-api (bare untyped strings) and dashboard-web (a local type), with no compiler tie between the two independently-deployed apps -- the exact structural shape that let a real backend error get mislabeled expired during the 2026-08-19 production incident. Fixed by promoting a single AuthErrorReason type into packages/shared-types, matching the existing AuthMethod/HealthStatus/SessionRevocationReason precedent -- GoogleAuthController now routes all three redirects through a typed redirectToAuthError() helper; dashboard-web's /auth/exchange route imports the shared type instead of a local copy; /auth/error's REASON_MESSAGES is now typed Record<AuthErrorReason, string> via a new isKnownReason() guard, so the file won't compile if a reason is ever added without a matching message. No behavior change for any real request intended -- a type-safety-only refactor. Independent code review (high effort, 8 finder angles) verified 7 candidates individually: 2 CONFIRMED (isKnownReason() used the `in` operator, which walks the prototype chain, so ?reason=constructor on the public, unauthenticated /auth/error page resolved to an inherited Object.prototype function value instead of a string, crashing the page render -- fixed with Object.hasOwn(); and the unrecognized-reason fallback logged nothing, undercutting the fix's own goal of catching cross-deploy drift between dashboard-api and dashboard-web's independently-deployed Vercel projects -- fixed with a console.error on that path only), 3 PLAUSIBLE (a narrow reason="" behavior change reachable only via a hand-typed URL; a redirectToAuthError name collision between the new dashboard-api controller method and the pre-existing dashboard-web route function; and the incident narrative restated across all 4 changed files' doc comments), 2 REFUTED (widening dashboard-web's route-local AuthErrorReason from 2 values to 3 -- an acceptable, even necessary side effect of the actual fix; and the new redirectToAuthError being a private class method rather than a standalone function -- the more idiomatic NestJS pattern given it needs this.env). gates.notes: Consolidated session-exchange debt closure (branch fix-remaining-session-exchange-debt, PR #38). Closes every remaining accepted-debt item from PR #36's and PR #37's own second-role reviews of the Google SSO session-exchange feature, bundled into one branch per explicit 'do it all together' instruction rather than repeating the review/gate/merge cycle per item. Two scoping decisions made directly with the user before building: Roadmap items omit `status` from the edit form (the backend silently strips it on generic update; only setActivePhase() may change it) and instead get a "Set as active phase"/"Clear active phase" action wired to the existing POST /projects/:projectId/active-phase; all four resources shipped together in one PR, matching the Team+Approvers precedent. Independent code review (high effort, 8 finder angles) surfaced 13 candidates -- 12 CONFIRMED, 1 REFUTED and dropped (a claimed sequenceStyle minWidth regression, where the visual change was real but caused by the markup restructuring itself, not the dropped property). 10 findings kept in the final report per the review's own cap, all 10 fixed and re-validated: the active-phase set/clear action previously updated only activePhaseId, never the affected roadmap items' own status, leaving a stale/contradictory StatusBadge until refresh -- now mirrors the backend's own status transaction locally; clearing a repository's Default branch field while editing silently reset it to "main" instead of preserving or blocking -- the field is now required and part of the edit form's validity check; a non-empty but unparseable Sequence value silently serialized to null via JSON.stringify's NaN handling -- a new parseSequence() helper rejects it client-side with a clear message; the active-phase response was cast to the wrong shared type (ApiSuccessResponse<ProjectDetail> instead of the backend's actual ApiSuccessResponse<ProjectEntity>) -- replaced with an honest, narrow local type; open inline edit forms never resynced on a concurrent external update, risking a silent lost-update on save -- fixed with a useEffect keyed on (id, updatedAt) narrow enough not to wipe an in-progress unsaved edit on an unrelated refresh; two real CSS regressions from the original page.tsx-to-component extraction (a dropped item-label min-width floor, and secondary text shrinking from the sm to xs token, undocumented) were both restored; router.refresh() on every mutation across all four new sections had raised the page's mutation-triggered full-refetch surfaces from 3 to 7 -- removed entirely where nothing else reads the data, and scoped to only fire on a roadmap edit when the edited item is the active phase; the markPending/pending-Set CRUD-handler pattern, reimplemented nearly verbatim across all four new components, was extracted into a new shared lib/use-pending-ids.ts hook; and the next/headers client-bundle fix (a second occurrence of a bug class already hit once before) was made proactive rather than reactive by extracting the remaining pure exports of lib/projects.ts into a new lib/projects-query.ts. 24 new/updated regression tests added (189/189 dashboard-web unit tests, up from 186); one planned test (the NaN-sequence guard via a real number input) was found unreproducible in jsdom -- its own value sanitization already clamps any non-finite value to "" at the DOM level -- recorded explicitly rather than dropped silently, with the code fix itself confirmed correct at the code level during the review's own verification pass. gates.notes: dashboard-web file upload on the Business Knowledge Record create form (branch dashboard-web-attachments-on-create, not yet pushed/opened as a PR). Closes the last named gap on the Business Knowledge Center module by letting a user pick attachments directly on the New record form, not only after the record already exists -- an attachment's record_id is a real database foreign key, so picked files are staged client-side and uploaded via the existing uploadAttachment() flow only once the record is actually created. No new backend surface; a new lib/business-knowledge-attachments.ts extracts the shared MIME/size allowlist and upload()-then-confirm() sequence out of the pre-existing detail-page control so the new picker reuses it instead of duplicating it. Independent code review (high effort, 9 finder angles, 1-vote verification) surfaced 8 kept findings -- all 8 came back CONFIRMED (0 PLAUSIBLE, 0 REFUTED) and all 8 were fixed. Most severe: handleSubmit had no internal guard against being re-invoked once the record was already created -- the <form> stayed mounted with the Title field the only remaining input that doesn't block HTML's implicit-submission-on-Enter behavior, so pressing Enter there after a partial upload failure could silently create a duplicate record; fixed with a real early-return guard inside handleSubmit itself, not just the button-swap the initial build relied on. Also fixed: the 'View record' link was clickable before staged uploads actually finished, letting a click mid-upload hard-navigate and silently abort in-flight uploads with no error surfaced; the batch-upload path never checked for AttachmentUploadApiError, discarding curated backend rejection reasons in favor of a generic message; pendingFiles was never trimmed after a partial success; attachmentError was never cleared on submit; a doc comment contradicted the actual navigation behavior; and a hand-copied CSS rule was missing a :disabled state. 5 new regression tests added. Security review (run separately) found 0 findings above threshold -- confirmed this diff is client-side UI/orchestration only, no new backend endpoint, no changes to the upload-route proxy/RBAC/HTML-sanitization boundary; the Blob-pathname-from-raw-filename construction was verified via git show to be byte-for-byte identical to the pre-existing, already-reviewed code this refactor only relocated. Built using Service Library as the literal structural template (same service_persona_proof RBAC group, no new RBAC migration). Two scoping decisions confirmed directly with the user first (AskUserQuestion): content edits stay independent of approvalStatus, mirroring Service Library's own precedent; and Service Library's own icpIds field is not retrofitted to a real relationship in this pass -- Persona Library stays fully standalone (relatedServiceIds is a plain, existence-validated identifier array, not a foreign key). Built by a background agent, then independently re-verified by the orchestrating session -- a first delegation attempt returned only a plan with zero real file changes, caught via a direct git status check before being trusted; the second attempt, with a more directive prompt, did the real work, and every test suite the agent reported was independently re-run and confirmed, not just trusted.
